messages:
Priya (PM): dropping a quick thread for the onboarding UI review. Fig dropped: https://www.figma.com/file/efgh5678/onboard-v3
Priya (PM): key decision: compact bottom rail (pills) vs full-width sticky banner for first-run quickstarts. we want higher activation but avoid being annoying. need copy + a11y feedback.

Elaine (Designer): pills = low visual weight, sits above footer. banner = obvious and supports richer content (sample picker + brief description). pills could expand to a tray.

Jon (UX): data point: earlier cohort had 18% activation with small CTA. hypothesis: a more prominent banner could push that to 25-30%. but risk survey feedback saying "too pushy". propose test with qualitative intercept.

Mike (Frontend): implementation notes: banner simpler (single component). pills require a small expand/collapse animation and persistent per-workspace state. both need keyboard traps handled.

Sofia (Accessibility): accessibility checklist highlights:
- color contrast for pill text fails at small sizes in dark theme (use semantic tokens)
- ensure expand/collapse is aria-expanded and keyboard focusable
- focus order: close button should be before secondary links to match expected focus path
- provide skip link to avoid cognitive load for screen reader users

Sam (Devex): analytics to track: onboard_variant (pill|banner), shown_ts, interacted (open/sample/skip), dismiss_reason. will add to tracking doc and include experiment id.

Elaine (Designer): copy variations to try:
A) Headline: "Try a sample project"  CTA: "Open"  Secondary: "Skip"
B) Headline: "Get started with a sample" CTA: "Try it" Secondary: "No thanks"
C) Headline: "Start building in seconds" CTA: "Use sample" Secondary: "Later"
Which tone do we want? friendly vs imperative?

Priya (PM): prefer friendly — lean A or B. target users are devs; keep verbs short. also important: microcopy under the title should say what the sample demonstrates (e.g., chat, embeddings).

Jon (UX): microcopy idea: include estimated time: "5 min setup" — that increases conversions in experiments. show small tag in the pill/banner.

Sofia (Accessibility): if you show "5 min", ensure semantically it's not the only accessible cue. screen readers need a descriptive label like "Sample: Chatbot demo, approx 5 minutes".

Mike (Frontend): CSS sketch for tray expand animation:
```css
.onboard-pill { position: fixed; right: 16px; bottom: 24px; z-index: 50; }
.onboard-tray { transition: transform .18s ease; transform-origin: bottom right; }
```
Also: for banner, set role="region" and aria-label="Onboarding quickstart".

Sam (Devex): feature-flagging plan: default to pill for 100% internal, banner for 25% external A variant. flag key: onboarding_ui_variant. will coordinate rollout windows and metric gates (activation + NPS).

Priya (PM): privacy note: don't show quickstart until we've surfaced telemetry opt-in. Marcus raised this in infra sync; we should respect opt-out.

Elaine (Designer): updated frames: I'll post two prototypes (pill collapsed + banner expanded) with contrast values and copy variants by tomorrow. will include mobile breakpoint tweaks.

Sofia (Accessibility): quick checklist for the PR: semantic tokens, aria-live polite announcement on show, skip link, aria-expanded toggles, proper focus return on close. I'll review once PR is up.

Mike (Frontend): i'll flip DOM order so dismiss button comes first for keyboard users and add role/button semantics. will open draft PR by Tuesday.

Sam (Devex): tracking doc updated: https://notion.so/redwood/onboard-experiments — added events + experiment id mapping.

launch-bot: reminder: run accessibility smoke tests and e2e after UI changes.

Priya (PM): actions: Elaine update frames + include "5 min" microcopy; Sofia review PR; Mike PR; Sam add events and experiment; Jon set up intercept for qualitative. target milestone: Wednesday design review + Friday small internal canary. :rocket:

Elaine (Designer): noted — will include both copy tones A+B. thanks.

Priya (PM): thanks team, ping here for blockers.
